Subject: Post-demo: deployment boundary assessment & next steps

Hi Sara / Jake / Kauri team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation and very helpful context on the triage workflow and PHI handling requirements. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from call:
- Primary workload: near-real-time patient triage (low-latency responses for clinician-facing UI).
- Data residency constraint: Kauri legal reiterated that patient-identifying records must not leave NZ or the EU (depending on country), and cross-border routing requires explicit contracts / data flow approvals.
- Volume: steady 60–80 req/s peak per region, bursts up to ~200 for influx windows.
- Tolerance: sub-300ms tail for generation paths is a stated SLO for clinical UX.

Implications for hosting options:
- Hosted API (fastest): We have eu-west region with full residency support for EU customer data. APAC coverage is currently SG (ap-southeast-1) — we do not operate a NZ region today. Hosted could work if Kauri accepts processing in SG under a contractual data transfer mechanism or if you restrict residency to EU only.
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pools can be provisioned in AWS Sydney (ap-southeast-2) to keep processing in APAC with predictable throughput. This is a common middle-ground for customers prioritizing regional processing with shorter lead times than on-prem.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full private control plane (VPC or on-prem package) is possible but will require a longer provisioning timeline (4–10+ weeks depending on on-prem ops) and deeper security review. It gives the strongest guarantees for locked-down residency.

Attachments & links:
- Attached: redwood_region_matrix_v1.pdf (matrix of regions, latency expectations, and rough provisioning timelines).
- Shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/kauri-health-region-matrix

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the strictness of the residency requirement: is it strictly "data cannot leave NZ at any point" for NZ patients, or is contractual cross-border processing acceptable with controls?
2) If NZ hard-residency: we should schedule a technical workshop to scope Private/on-prem vs Dedicated in Sydney and capture exact network/integration constraints (CTO + infra).
3) If contractual cross-border is acceptable: we can follow up with a pricing sketch for Dedicated in Sydney vs Hosted SG and include latency/cost tradeoffs.

I can coordinate a 60-min technical workshop with Ben (infra) and Marissa (compliance) this week or next. What times work for you?

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Residency: For NZ patients the rule is strict — PHI must remain within NZ borders unless we have an approved Data Transfer Agreement AND a technical control that ensures data residency (we're evaluating whether contractual controls alone are sufficient).
- APAC expectation: We are piloting in NZ and Australia simultaneously; if we can get a dedicated capacity in Sydney that avoids crossing into SG or the US that would be ideal.
- Timeline & cost sensitivity: We are on a compressed timeline — CTO needs a workable architecture decision by end of month. We need a ballpark cost and lead time for Dedicated in Sydney vs Private VPC/On-prem so we can evaluate procurement.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support Dedicated capacity in ap-southeast-2 (Sydney) and what lead times look like? If Private on-prem is realistic, please include an early estimate for effort (weeks + typical cost ranges).

Thanks — will loop Jake in for scheduling the workshop.

—Sara Lin
Head of Product, Kauri Health
[sara.lin@kaurihealth.com]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-08T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment boundary assessment & next steps

Hi Sara — Ben here (Solutions Lead), thanks for the clarity. Short answers: 

- Dedicated in Sydney: Yes — we can provision Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) in ap-southeast-2. Typical lead time to get a baseline pool configured and tested is 2–4 weeks depending on sizing and network connectivity (VPC peering / transit setup).
- Private (on-prem / air-gapped) option: Absolutely supported but longer: 6–12 weeks is typical for on-prem engagements (includes infra validation, image signing, compliance checks). If you want a VPC Private deployment (customer VPC with our private control plane), that usually sits between Hosted and full on-prem and runs ~4–6 weeks.
- Ballpark cost ranges (very high level): Dedicated pool (Sydney) starting ~$20k–$40k/month depending on instance size and commit; Private VPC is higher due to setup fees (pilot-level ~$60k–$120k one-time + ongoing ops fees). I will get finance to produce more precise numbers once we have sizing.

Next recommended actions: 
1) Tech workshop (60–90m) next Tue/Wed preferred — propose Tue 9–11am AEST / Wed 8–10am NZT. Diego and I will bring an infra runbook; Marissa will cover compliance boundaries and required docs (SOC2 evidence, DPA templates).
2) We will circulate a tightened timeline & estimate for both Dedicated (Sydney) and Private VPC by EOW after the workshop.

@Marissa — can you prepare the standard compliance packet and a rough SOW template we can share post-workshop?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
